title: Feature flags are not just on/off switches
subtitle: Release safely without redeploying every change
learning_objective: Explain how feature flags support gradual rollout and identify risks from stale flags.

scenes.title: SHIP WITHOUT EXPOSING EVERYONE
scenes.body: A new checkout flow is deployed, but you want to enable it for 1% of users before a wider rollout.

scenes.title: Separate deploy from release
scenes.body: A feature flag lets a running system choose between behaviors based on configuration or user attributes. It can support gradual exposure and quick disablement.

scenes.title: Flags create maintenance debt
scenes.body: Remove temporary flags after rollout, define safe defaults, and ensure authorization never depends only on a client-controlled feature flag.

scenes.question: What is a major benefit of a release feature flag?
options: It eliminates the need for testing
It separates deployment from exposure to users
It guarantees a rollback is never needed
scenes.explanation: The code can be deployed while exposure is controlled separately, enabling staged rollout and fast disablement.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Use flags to manage exposure deliberately—and assign owners and cleanup dates.
